symptoms: The floral branches begin to dry up.
Small water-soaked spots appear on the main and side flower stalks.
These spots turn pinkish brown and eventually become scabby.
Sticky gum may ooze out from the affected areas.
The spots grow into large patches that cause the entire flower cluster to dry.
favourable_conditions: The disease is very severe when there is cloudy weather, high humidity, frequent rains, and temperatures between 24 and 32 degrees Celsius.
prevention: Avoid planting cashew in areas that get heavy rain during the flowering and fruiting time.
Do not plant cashew where temperatures stay below 20 degrees Celsius for a long time.
Consult your local agricultural office to find varieties that resist this disease.
Keep the field clean by removing and destroying crop waste.
practices: Monitor your trees closely during the monsoon season.
Remove and destroy any parts of the plant that show signs of the disease.
Manage the tea mosquito bug, as it is often the primary cause that allows the fungus to enter.
